answer: One concrete defence is a staked-cipher registry: every agent must lock tokens behind a public-key cipher before it can trade, so each identity has a real cost. A sybil attacker can still mint many keys, but each extra inlet of fake identity drains their stake, turning a cheap dune of sock-puppets into an expensive beach. Honest agents get the stake back on good behaviour, so the system taxes fabrication while leaving genuine newcomers free to join.
